beats.say: An attacker does not always need a computer. A document left on a desk or an unlocked screen is enough.
Lock your screen whenever you stand up. On a Windows computer, press the Windows key and the letter L together.
If a stranger tries to follow you through a secured door, politely ask them to use their own badge.
Visitors sign in, wear a visitor badge and are always escorted in the building.

nodes.text: Could you hold the door, please? My hands are full. My badge is in my bag, I'm here to fix the printer.
nodes.speaker: Unknown man
nodes.spoken: Could you hold the door, please? My hands are full. <breath> My badge is in my bag, I'm here to fix the printer.

choices.label: Hold the door, his hands are full
choices.feedback: An unverified person got in. Attackers count on exactly this politeness.

choices.label: Offer to hold the boxes so he can find his badge
Let the door close and walk away silently
choices.feedback: He did not get in, but someone else may open the door. Telling security is better.

nodes.text: Looks like, I left it at home. I'm in a hurry, your boss is waiting for me.
nodes.speaker: Unknown man
nodes.spoken: Looks like, uh, I left it at home. I'm in a hurry, your boss is waiting for me.

choices.label: Fine, go ahead
choices.feedback: Naming the boss and rushing you is the oldest trick. No badge, no entry.

choices.label: Walk him to the security desk
choices.feedback: Right. They can issue a visitor badge or turn him away.

nodes.text: No printer repair is booked for today. Good thing you brought him here.
nodes.speaker: Security guard
nodes.spoken: No printer repair is booked for today. <breath> Good thing you brought him here.

choices.label: Also send a short note to the security team
choices.feedback: Well done. They will review cameras and check other entrances.

scenes.title: Call from reception
scenes.intro: The reception desk is calling you. Decide what to do about a visitor you did not expect.

actions.label: Answer
actions.feedback: Answer it. You decide about the visitor.

actions.label: Decline
actions.feedback: The desk gets no answer and may let the visitor through unchecked. Take such calls.

steps.say: Hello, there is an air conditioning technician here. He says you, excuse me, called him. Shall I send him up?
steps.spoken: Hello, <breath> there is an, uh, air conditioning technician here. He says you <cough> excuse me, called him. Shall I send him up?

actions.label: Yes, send him up
actions.feedback: An unchecked person will walk the building alone. Check the job order first.

actions.label: I did not call anyone, keep him at the desk
actions.feedback: Right. An unexpected visitor does not get in without a check.

actions.label: I will come down and see
actions.feedback: Good. Meet the visitor at the desk and do not leave him alone.

steps.say: He says Mr Kamran approved it. He only needs five minutes in the server room.
steps.spoken: He says <breath> Mr Kamran approved it. He only needs five minutes in the server room.

actions.label: Then let him in
actions.feedback: Unchecked access to the server room is a serious threat. A manager's name is not permission.

actions.label: I check the order with facilities
actions.feedback: Right. Check the order through official channels, not the visitor's word.

actions.label: I will call Mr Kamran myself
actions.feedback: Good. Call your manager on the number you know and ask.

steps.label: The call has ended. Facilities say no technician was booked today.

actions.label: Tell the guards and the security team
actions.feedback: Great. The guards will hold the person and the cameras will be checked.

actions.label: Do nothing
actions.feedback: The fake technician may try another entrance. Reporting protects the building.

question.prompt: You are going to lunch. What must not stay on your desk?

options.label: A sticky note with a password
options.feedback: A password should never sit on paper in plain sight.

options.label: A folder with a citizen's application
options.feedback: Put confidential files in a locked cabinet.

options.label: An unlocked work phone
options.feedback: An unlocked phone opens the door to your accounts.

options.label: An empty coffee cup
options.feedback: That is not a risk. Just tidy it up.

scenes.explain: Clean desk rule: when you leave, papers, media and devices are locked away.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation with the right reaction.

pairs.left: A stranger without a badge in the corridor
pairs.right: Politely ask and guide them to security
Return it to the owner without reading
Report it at once so it gets blocked

pairs.left: A colleague left their screen unlocked

scenes.explain: Physical security is everyone's job. A small step prevents a big leak.

scenes.prompt: Put a visitor's arrival in order.

items.label: The visitor signs in at reception
Gets a visitor badge and wears it visibly
The host meets and escorts them
The badge is returned on the way out

scenes.explain: A visitor is never left alone in the building and hands the badge back on leaving.

points: Lock your screen when you stand up and keep papers locked away.
Do not let strangers follow you in, send them to security.
Collect prints at once and destroy confidential paper properly.
